title: Conditional reward scope research for a 100-upstream contribution campaign
source_method: Read-only GitHub connector REST repository metadata and repository file observations; official program pages for supplementary opportunity screening.
limitations: These 100 unique repository identities are a researched pool, not 100 ready tasks, submissions, accepted contributions or paid engagements.
Scope verification does not establish a security benefit, personal eligibility, maintainer acceptance, bounty selection or entitlement to payment.
No target-specific contribution or AI policy is treated as reviewed until an actual task is selected.
Non-archived repository metadata does not prove maintainer availability. Activity and competing solutions must be rechecked when selecting work.

This is an initial curated sample of the program scope, not its complete list. The OSS-Fuzz directory response was limited to its first 1000 entries; each included integration file was fetched individually.

programs.name: Google Patch Rewards
programs.base_award_interpretation: Category assignment and all payment decisions belong to the rewards panel; no amount is estimated for any project or candidate patch.
programs.temporary_multiplier_note: The rules advertise noncumulative 2026 memory-safety multipliers for qualifying Tier 1 work, excluding S3. No candidate is assumed to qualify.
acceptance_conditions: Demonstrate a substantive security improvement in an in-scope upstream.
Follow the upstream's coding, testing and contribution requirements; obtain acceptance and retain it without reverts for one full month before applying.
Submit at most three program reports per person per month; batch related commits. Patches over twelve months old are normally ineligible.
Existing OSS-Fuzz integration supports Tier 2 scope. New integrations and fuzz harnesses are excluded.
Reactive fixes are considered individually; simple non-exploitable crash or resource-exhaustion fixes generally do not qualify.
programs.participant_boundaries: Age/adult-submitter, location, sanctions, payment and legal conditions apply; this research does not determine the user's eligibility.
programs.payment_conditions: Discretionary panel approval; an award may be shared with maintainers. No payment is guaranteed.

actionable_gaps.title: Parameterized array comparison misses a VARCHAR row after an index is added

reported_reproduction.runtime: In-memory H2 through the public JDBC API; no service, credentials or production data required.
reported_reproduction.query_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM T WHERE V = ANY(?)

actionable_gaps.source_observation: At the pinned revision, ConditionInArray.createIndexConditions adds a parameter-based index condition without the Comparison.isSafeIndexCondition checks used for constant and other array expressions.

competing_solution_check.observation: No corresponding solution observed in all 47 current open PRs or the 100 most recently updated closed PRs. The issue timeline returned no cross-reference events.
competing_solution_check.related_change_note: The older merged lossy-conversion index fix may inform analysis; it does not establish that the currently reported parameter-array case is solved.

next_validation: Reproduce indexed versus unindexed results at the exact source revision before changing code.
Test scalar and array parameter values, incompatible comparison types, NULL and empty arrays, and prepared-statement reuse with changed parameter types.
Add an upstream regression in the existing Java or SQL test suite and show it fails before the patch.
Preserve valid index use; examine the effect on query plans and same-type comparisons.
Run H2's documented build and relevant tests, coverage, formatting and changelog checks before preparing a submission.

contribution_policy.summary: Java 11-compatible code, established style, integrated regression tests, coverage of changed code, full test run and changelog are required by the guide.
contribution_policy.authorship_requirement: The guide requests a specific authorship/licensing statement for significant contributions. It must only be made when truthful.
contribution_policy.ai_policy_observation: No specific AI policy found in the inspected root, .github, README and official build guide; this is not blanket permission.

benefit_assessment.explanation: A useful correctness fix can support the contribution portfolio. Scope alone does not show that this particular issue meets Patch Rewards security criteria.

parked_candidates.reason: The pending-surrogate reset defect already has an open fix and regression PR; duplicating it would not be distinct work.
parked_candidates.reopen_when: Maintainers or review establish a specific uncovered behavior or request independent validation with a defined useful result.

parked_candidates.reason: The ignored allow_overwrite option in multi-value flags is documented in an open issue, but copying the scalar guard would break ordinary repeated-flag use. A maintainer must choose the intended API semantics.
parked_candidates.reopen_when: Upstream selects rejection at definition, explicit documentation, or tracking distinct parsing passes. Then implement the agreed behavior and regressions.

notes: No three currently selectable cash opportunities could be established from the checked primary sources.
HuskSync advertises a generic code-bounty system in its README, but current per-issue funding, acceptance and payment terms were not verified; it is not counted as paid work.
Algora's Cal.com board shows two open amounts on the same font-weight issue; they are not two distinct programming tasks.
Previously rejected, crowded, expired or already-rewarded offers were not reopened without new evidence.
